what: When the four acceptance suites were last put to a REAL `claude`, and the day this repository stops believing that they still would pass.

WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. From Ш32 those suites run against `tests/acceptance/fake-claude/`, a double built out of what this repository believes about Claude Code. Nothing in a run against the double can check that belief: a wrong guess in the double becomes a green test that certifies the guess, and a green test that certifies a guess is worse than no test, because it reads as cover. The only instrument that checks the belief is the real CLI, and running it spends the owner's money -- so it is not automated, it is OWED, and this file is the debt.

WHAT MAKES IT IMPOSSIBLE TO FORGET. `tests/fake-claude.test.ts` reads this file and goes red when the debt is overdue. That suite is in the UNIT run, which is in `gate:fast`, which is what `tools/pre-push.sh` runs -- so the day this expires, nothing leaves the machine until somebody deals with it. The form is `gate/allowed-red.json`'s, deliberately: an admission with a name on it, a reason, and a day it stops working.
WHAT THE OWNER HAS TO DO, when it goes red. Run the four suites against the real CLI, by hand, on a machine logged into an account they mean to spend:

and again with $env:GRIPTERM_ACCEPTANCE_ENGINE = 'own'. What it costs is one turn on the account for П2 and one `--resume` per sitting after it; `rename` and П3 spend nothing. Then write the day, the CLI build it ran against, the engines, and the verdict into `lastRun` below, and set `grace` to null.

WHAT TO DO IF IT DISAGREES WITH THE DOUBLE. The disagreement is the finding, and it is worth more than the run. Every behaviour the double copies is listed in the header of `fake-claude.mjs` with the measurement it came from; a suite that passes against the real CLI and fails against the double, or the other way round, names the belief that moved. Correct the double, not the suite.

WHAT `lastRun: null` MEANS. That the Ш32 executor did not establish it. The step was forbidden to start a real `claude` even once -- the whole point of it was to stop spending the owner's account -- so it could not run the suites against one, and it does not know when anybody last did. A date invented here would have been the exact defect this file exists to prevent, so the field is null and the grace below carries the pressure instead. THAT STATEMENT IS NOW HALF FALSE AND KEPT FOR THE RECORD: a real CLI has been met since, on 2026-09-08, and what it said is the next paragraph.

FIRST CONTACT WITH THE REAL CLI, 2026-09-08, AND IT CAME BACK RED. One of the four criteria -- `rename`, the one this file`s own instructions say spends nothing -- was run against the real `claude` 2.1.260 on this machine, under both engines. Under `own` no session reached `idle` inside 90 s, twice out of twice. Under `editor` a session reached `idle` in under 15 s and then `/rename` never reached the row inside 90 s. The same criterion against the double is green in about 4 s on both engines. BOTH CAUSES WERE ESTABLISHED THE SAME DAY, and this paragraph used to say they were not. Under `own`: the suites answered the CLI`s trust prompt with a bare Enter, and the prompt`s cursor starts on `No, exit` -- so this repository was telling Claude Code to leave, and reporting that as a session which never started. Under `editor`: `/rename` reached the CLI and the CLI renamed the conversation; what refused it was OURS. `readSessionName` REJECTED any session file carrying `nameSource` at all, because on 2026-08-13 against 2.1.228 `/rename` REMOVED that key and its absence was the only evidence a person had chosen the name. In 2.1.260 the key is always present and carries the answer -- `derived` or `user` -- so a rule written to admit a person`s name was refusing every name there is. FIXED THE SAME DAY: `user` is admitted, an absent key still is, `derived` and anything unknown are not. WHETHER THAT FIXED WHAT THE OWNER SAW WAS LEFT TO A HAND, because this file could not answer it: the acceptance meets a double, and the double was taught the new shape from the same measurement, so a green from it could not be the evidence. THE HAND ANSWERED THE SAME EVENING. The owner opened a real editor on a real `claude` 2.1.260 under `own`, typed `/rename test`, and `test` arrived on the panel tab, on the row and in the details header. That is the strongest link this repository has ever had on this behaviour, and the run below is the second.

TWO THINGS THAT RUN ESTABLISHED ABOUT THE INSTRUMENT, AND BOTH WERE CLOSED THE SAME DAY. It found that the double did not model the CLI`s trust prompt AT ALL and said so in its own head -- so every green these four suites had ever shown was shown by a program that skipped the first question a real CLI asks about a folder it has not seen. And it found that the line all four printed -- answering the CLI trust prompt with Enter -- was a GUESS rather than a sighting: printed whenever no session appeared within 15 s, with nothing here ever looking at the screen, although under `own` the product holds the bytes. NEITHER IS TRUE ANY MORE (Ш38 and Ш39): the suites read the tail and answer only what they have seen, and refuse rather than guess where there is no screen to read; the double asks the question in the form measured that day, so the answering path is walked by every acceptance run under `own` instead of by the rare paid one. WHAT REMAINS TRUE, and is why this file exists: both of those were THIS REPOSITORY`S beliefs about somebody else`s program, and one run against the real thing is what found them.

WALKED AGAIN THE SAME DAY, AND IT PASSED. After the three fixes -- the instrument answers what it has seen, the double asks the question, and `readSessionName` admits `user` -- `rename` was run once more against the real `claude` 2.1.260 under `own`. The instrument said `the cursor is on -No, exit-; sending a Down arrow`, then `the cursor is on -Yes, I trust this folder-; confirming`, and then: `project -> gripterm-acceptance-renamed on the row, in the record and on our own tab`, 22.4 s -- with the other direction behind it, a name given here reaching Claude Code`s own session file, 6.4 s. THAT IS THE FIRST TIME ANY OF THESE FOUR CRITERIA HAS PASSED AGAINST CLAUDE CODE ITSELF, and it is the answer to a defect the owner had found by hand an hour earlier: he typed `/rename` into a real CLI and the row kept its old name.

WHY `lastRun` IS STILL null AFTER THAT RUN, and it is deliberate rather than forgotten. `tests/fake-claude.test.ts` computes the deadline as `lastRun.on` plus `maxAgeDays`, so writing today into it would push this debt out to 2026-10-08 -- a month bought with ONE criterion of four, which FAILED. That is the exact defect this file exists to prevent. The grace of 2026-09-14 stands untouched, and what the run bought instead is written above. AND IT IS STILL null AFTER THE GREEN ONES, for the same arithmetic sharpened by the paragraph above: two criteria of four, and they are the two that cost nothing. П2 and О1 -- the two that spend an account -- are exactly the two not walked, so a date written today would buy thirty days for the half of this debt that is free. THE OTHER HALF OF THE SAME ARITHMETIC, AND IT IS THE PART A FUTURE READER WILL BE TEMPTED BY: `rename` and П3 are also the two whose greens have now been earned against Claude Code itself, which makes writing the date feel more defensible than it is. It is not more defensible. `maxAgeDays` is a claim about the WHOLE acceptance, and half of it has still never met the real CLI in this repository`s history. The grace of 2026-09-14 stands untouched, and what it buys is a paid run of П2 and О1 at a time of the owner`s choosing.

BOTH ENGINES, TWO CRITERIA, GREEN -- 2026-09-08, AND THIS IS THE WIDEST THIS ACCEPTANCE HAS EVER BEEN AGAINST THE REAL THING. Run by the orchestrator with `GRIPTERM_ACCEPTANCE_AGENT=real` against `claude` 2.1.260, after the `nameSource` fix. Under `editor`, `rename`: all THREE of its suites, 44 s -- the row and the record, the tab the editor draws, and a name given here reaching Claude Code`s own session file (8388, 8402, 8572 ms). Under `editor`, П3: 13 s, and the conversation really did change underneath the record (`a780ef4e... -> 942d0b0a...`). Under `own`, the same two criteria, 54 s, with `rename from the CLI reaches an editor tab` excluded by name as it always is there. FIVE HOSTS, NO RED, NOTHING SKIPPED THAT WAS NOT SKIPPED ON PURPOSE.

WHAT THOSE FIVE HOSTS DID NOT WALK, said here because a green is only as wide as what it touched. NONE OF THEM ANSWERED THE TRUST QUESTION. There is no `the cursor is on ...` line anywhere in their output and each terminal came up in about 8 s instead of the 22.4 s the same machine measured that morning -- the real CLI had already recorded trust for the acceptance folder during the earlier run of the same day, into the profile of whoever ran it, which is a cost this repository writes down and does not tidy. So the path Ш39 built, and the reason the earlier run went red, was NOT exercised by these five; what exercises it is a first run against a folder the CLI has not seen, and against the double on every `own` run. And П2 and О1 were not run at all.
whyThatMany: Thirty days, and it is measured rather than chosen for roundness: this repository's own notes carry `claude` moving from 2.1.224 to 2.1.245 between 2026-08-10 and 2026-08-27, which is twenty-one patch builds in seventeen days. Against a CLI moving at that rate a belief a month old is already about a build nobody is running. Longer would make the check decorative; shorter would make it a chore that gets its date pushed instead of its run done.

grace.why: The double was built on 2026-08-31 and has never been compared with the thing it doubles. Two weeks is the room the executor took to let the owner schedule a paid run at a time of their choosing rather than the moment they next push. `ratifiedBy: null` means what it means in `gate/allowed-red.json`: nobody but the agent that wrote this line has agreed to it, and the owner has not been asked.
